title: Digital 3D — Shared Contracts
summary: Shared JSON schemas, a canonical coordinate frame and a framework-agnostic viewer kernel that let independently owned 3D modules, such as a bridge twin and a district twin, work together.

narrative.problem: Independently owned 3D modules, such as a bridge model and a neighbourhood model, must agree on where things are, which vertical datum is zero, how levels of detail relate and what one module may know about another; otherwise a bridge authored against mean high water can sit 0.59 m into buildings authored against NAVD88.
narrative.decision: The repository holds no module data, only normative JSON Schema 2020-12 contracts, a frozen canonical scene frame that modules copy byte-for-byte, and a framework-agnostic viewer kernel; every level of detail from every module is placed on one max_geometric_error_m axis.
narrative.tradeoff: Freezing the frame anchor and allowing only additions within a major version keeps every module's coordinates stable, but the anchor cannot be corrected for the life of contract version 1, and removing anything must wait for a new major version.
narrative.limitation: The bundled fixtures are tiny and synthetic and exist only to self-test the schemas; the contracts are consumed so far by two sibling modules, manhattan-bridge-3d and dumbo-district-3d, and the repository has no hosted demo of its own.

images.alt: Document excerpt card headed 'No module data' quoting the README: only the things that must be agreed once and used by everyone — schemas, their documents and the runtime packages both viewers consume.
images.caption: The repository's scope rule: it publishes agreements, not geometry, so modules depend on contracts rather than on each other's source.
images.credit: Excerpt from the Digital 3D Shared Contracts README

images.alt: Document excerpt card headed 'One frame' quoting the README on naming vertical datums so a bridge on mean high water does not sit 0.59 m into buildings on NAVD88.
images.caption: A shared, frozen scene frame with named vertical datums is what lets separately built modules line up.
images.credit: Excerpt from the Digital 3D Shared Contracts README

images.alt: Document excerpt card headed 'One LOD axis' quoting the README: a viewer mode is a different screen-space-error budget on the shared ladder, the difference between CAD inspection and a walkthrough.
images.caption: One level-of-detail axis lets the same viewer act as a CAD inspector or a district walkthrough without forking.
images.credit: Excerpt from the Digital 3D Shared Contracts README
